title: Hierarchical Latency Stack + Token Sankey for Model/Route Performance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a combined hierarchical latency-stack visualization and token-flow Sankey to help engineers and PMs inspect per-model and per-route performance. The intent is a single canvas panel that shows: 1) aggregated latency broken into service/kernel/queue/batch/compute buckets, 2) token flow from request ingress through routing, KV cache hits, model layers and response generation as an interactive Sankey, 3) per-bucket cost attribution and token counts, 4) filters by model version, route, time window, and percentile. This ticket covers visual specs, interaction states, accessibility considerations, and a high-fidelity Figma prototype for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma panel with desktop and narrow-breakpoint layouts submitted
Component spec sheet listing layers: queue, batch, kernel, decode, kv-cache with consistent color tokens
Interaction detail: hover tooltips, time-range scrub, percentile selector, compare-two-versions mode
Exportable chart specs (SVG + JSON mapping) and a lightweight demo gif for QA
Design sign-off from PM (Evan Liu) and staff-engineering review scheduled
design_notes: Place latency-stack as stacked bars at top (aggregates) with collapsible buckets; each bucket drills down to sample microtraces
Token Sankey sits below and aligns horizontally with latency buckets so hover on a bucket highlights the related Sankey flows
Color system: use hue A for latency buckets and hue B for token paths; ensure color-blind safe palette and contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for text
Percentile control (p50/p95/p99) toggles both stack heights and Sankey thickness; default p95
Sampling: Sankey should be built from sampled traces (configurable) with a small badge showing sampling rate and a link to raw trace explorer
Comparison mode: allow side-by-side or overlay of two model versions or two routes; overlay uses dashed outlines and split Sankey colors
Minimum viewport: adapt layout for 1024px width, hide microtrace inline and surface via modal on small screens
Performance: reduce node count in Sankey by grouping low-volume tokens into an "Other" node to keep rendering performant
Accessibility: keyboard focus should move between stack buckets and Sankey nodes; tooltip text available in ARIA live region
decisions: Use Sankey (token-flow) instead of chord diagrams because Sankey more naturally maps directional token movement across pipeline stages
Represent latency buckets as proportional stacked bars rather than stacked area to preserve precise bar comparisons across percentiles
Default to p95 for reliability-focused troubleshooting; expose p50 and p99 in the percentile toggle
Group kernel/compute details behind a collapse affordance to keep default view simple for non-engineering users
Prototype will use mocked backend endpoints; final implementation will accept a compact JSON shape (list of nodes and weighted links) to allow streaming updates
tradeoffs: Sankey fidelity vs performance: high-fidelity Sankeys become expensive at high cardinalities; we will limit nodes and surface sampling metadata instead
Inline microtraces increase context but add cognitive load; chose modal drill-down to preserve canvas clarity
Color grouping provides quick signal but reduces granularity for users who want per-kernel hue; will provide a toggle for 'detailed color' in advanced settings
Comparison overlay helps quick visual diffs but can be confusing when many flows intersect; provide explicit legend and per-flow highlight on hover
